vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: constraint-engine
Version: 1.3.1

The constraint-engine skill is a framework for managing agentic guardrails by generating and enforcing rules based on past failures. It operates entirely within the local workspace (output/constraints/ and output/hooks/), lacks network access, and focuses on safety-oriented logic such as circuit breakers and audit-logged overrides. No indicators of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or prompt injection were found in SKILL.md or _meta.json.

llm.summary: This skill is a local constraint-management aid that discloses its automatic checks, local file writes, and dependency needs, with no artifact evidence of exfiltration or hidden execution.

dimensions.detail: The skill states it operates inside the agent trust boundary, uses the configured model, writes results locally under output/constraints and output/hooks, and does not call external APIs.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses mutable OpenClaw package identifiers and includes an extra context-verifier install command in the dependency sequence, so users should verify dependency provenance or pin versions when possible.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The pre-action and threshold-based automatic triggers are broad and can block agent actions, but this behavior is central to the stated guardrail purpose and the skill documents override and lifecycle commands.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: It persists constraints and audit logs in workspace files, which is expected for enforcement history; no system-level persistence, scheduled tasks, environment variable access, or tool replacement is documented.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The documented purpose is to generate, check, lifecycle-manage, and enforce local constraints from prior failure observations; reading configuration, reading failure-memory observations, writing constraint files, and logging blocked actions fit that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you want the agent to maintain local guardrails that can automatically check or block actions. Review generated constraints before activating them, use overrides deliberately, and verify or pin the referenced dependencies if your environment requires stronger supply-chain control.
llm.findings:
[P3] unexpected: The referenced lines are a negative claim that the skill does not send data to external services; the artifact contains no instruction to transmit conversation or user data externally.
[E1] unexpected: The scanner matched denial text rather than an external transmission path; the skill explicitly says no network resources, external APIs, or third-party services are called.
[EA1] unexpected: The referenced lines say the skill does not execute arbitrary code, and the package contains only Markdown instructions with no executable component.
[SQP-1] expected: Automatic pre-action checking and threshold-based generation are disclosed and purpose-aligned for an enforcement skill, though the trigger criteria are broad enough that users should understand when it may intervene.
[T08] expected: The install commands are normal for a skill with dependencies, but they are not pinned to immutable versions and one helper dependency is shown in the install sequence without much explanation.
